required.quote: Any individual applying for licensure as an advanced practice registered nurse shall submit proof that he holds a current, unencumbered, unrestricted registered nurse license, has satisfactorily completed a formal education program preparing graduates to practice specialized and advanced nursing practice, and holds a current certification for advanced practice granted by a nationally recognized certifying agency

exams.name: Nursing licensure examination (registered nurse)
exams.notes: Applicant must pass an examination to the satisfaction of the board for initial RN licensure, which is a prerequisite for APRN licensure.
exams.quote: Passes an examination to the satisfaction of the board.

required.quote: The board shall require advanced practice registered nurses practicing family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics, or gynecology to complete a minimum of one hour of continuing education on nutrition and metabolic health every four years.

available.quote: The board may by endorsement issue a license to practice as an advanced practice registered nurse if the applicant has practiced as an advanced practice registered nurse under the laws of another state and, in the opinion of the board, has met the requirements of Paragraph (A)(2) of this Section.

requirements.value: Applicant must have practiced as an APRN under the laws of another state and, in the opinion of the board, met the APRN licensure requirements of RS 37:920(A)(2).

disciplinary_grounds.description: Selling, falsely obtaining, or furnishing any nursing diploma or license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Is guilty of selling or attempting to sell, falsely obtaining, or furnishing any nursing diploma or license to practice as a registered nurse.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of a crime reflecting inability to practice nursing with due regard for health and safety
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Is convicted of a crime or offense which reflects the inability of the nurse to practice nursing with due regard for the health and safety of clients or patients or enters a plea of guilty or nolo contendere to a criminal charge regardless of final disposition

disciplinary_grounds.description: Unfitness or incompetence by reason of negligence, habit, or other cause
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Is unfit or incompetent by reason of negligence, habit, or other cause.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Inability to practice with reasonable skill and safety due to alcohol, drugs, illness, or mental/physical condition
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has demonstrated actual or potential inability to practice nursing with reasonable skill and safety to individuals because of use of alcohol or drugs; or has demonstrated inability to practice nursing with reasonable skill and safety to individuals because of illness or as a result of any mental or physical condition.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding or abetting anyone in violation of the nursing practice act
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Is guilty of aiding or abetting anyone in the violation of any provisions of this Part.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having a nursing or other health care provider license denied, revoked, suspended, or otherwise restricted
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has had a license to practice nursing or to practice as another health care provider denied, revoked, suspended, or otherwise restricted.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of any provision of the nursing practice act
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has violated any provision of this Part.

definition_quote.value: Certified nurse midwife or "CNM" who is an advanced practice registered nurse educated in the disciplines of nursing and midwifery and certified according to a nationally recognized certifying body, such as the American College of Nurse Midwives Certification Council, as approved by the board and who is authorized to manage the nurse midwifery care of newborns and women in the antepartum, intrapartum, postpartum, and/or gynecological periods.
definition_quote.quote: Certified nurse midwife or "CNM" who is an advanced practice registered nurse educated in the disciplines of nursing and midwifery and certified according to a nationally recognized certifying body, such as the American College of Nurse Midwives Certification Council, as approved by the board and who is authorized to manage the nurse midwifery care of newborns and women in the antepartum, intrapartum, postpartum, and/or gynecological periods.
